egress.terms: 'unlimited bandwidth' per the page description; the accounts themselves are 'Active 1 Days' on the Singapore 1 and 5 servers, against 'up to 7 days' in the overview.; ingress: none

interface_detail: 'Port 22(OpenSSH)', '81,444-SSL(Dropbear)', 'Support UDP CUSTOM port 1-65535', 'Support SlowDNS', 'WebSocket CDN (Port 80)', '446,7200 BADVPN UDPGW'.

chaining: A one-day Singapore SSH account is a cheap way to test whether SSH remote forwarding is permitted, which would make it an ingress path that needs no card and no VM.

limits.value: 'Active 1 Days' on the Singapore 1 and 5 servers; 'up to 7 days' in the overview

binding_note: Bandwidth is stated unlimited, so volume does not bind. The one-day account life binds first, and the ingress test is not passed at all: the account is an outbound proxy, and SSH remote forwarding would need GatewayPorts enabled on the provider's host, which the page does not state.

identity_cost.detail: The page offers 'Create Username SSH Tunnel' and the site description says 'create username and password whatever you want'; no email confirmation is described on the page read.

reliability_note: Accounts reset daily at 21:00 GMT+7 and some servers are full; torrent is refused; the offering is ad-funded with affiliate links to DigitalOcean and Vultr.
confidence_note: Hosts, ports, account life and the unlimited-bandwidth sentence are on the page read on 2026-10-23.

evidence.proved: 'Free SSH Tunnel Singapore Servers', 'Active up to 7 days with unlimited bandwidth', 'Free SSH Tunnel will reset at 21:00 GMT+7'.
Server Singapore 1: 'sg1.vpnjantit.com', 'Port 22(OpenSSH)', 'Support UDP CUSTOM port 1-65535', 'BADVPN UDPGW', 'Active 1 Days', 'Provider DIGITALOCEAN'.

notes: The second Singapore data point and the cheaper shape of the same idea: a free SSH login on a DigitalOcean or Vultr host in Singapore, no email, one day. It is an outbound proxy. The interesting untested question is whether the host permits SSH remote forwarding, which would turn a free account into a TCP ingress without a user owning any hardware; that is a probe, not a read. Country of endpoint: Singapore. Operator: the same Indonesian account-generator network class as OpenTunnel. Several Singapore servers showed 'Server Full' at read time.

extras.wg_detail: An SSH login on a public Singapore address, not a WireGuard peer: no .conf is issued and a user does not control the host, so no WireGuard interface can be created on the far side.
extras.volume_stated: 'unlimited bandwidth' per the page description; the accounts themselves are 'Active 1 Days' on the Singapore 1 and 5 servers, against 'up to 7 days' in the overview.
extras.transit_note: A rented Singapore host (the page names DigitalOcean and Vultr) carries the bytes.
